claim: SamplesRead double-counts every subquery feeding a range-vector function: evalSubquery merges the child's SamplesRead into the parent via MergeSamplesReadFromSubquery, then replaces the SubqueryExpr with a MatrixSelector over the materialized result, and the range-vector loop counts every point of that matrix again via IncrementSamplesReadAtStep at engine.go:2184. rate(x[5m:1m]) reports read=10 vs total=5 (2x), nested subqueries 3.8x, and samplesRead exceeds totalQueryableSamples contrary to the docs added in the PR; the test at engine_test.go:1548 pins the overcount as expected.
raw: #1 🟠 High: `SamplesRead` double-counts every subquery feeding a range-vector function

claim: TotalSamples silently regresses for @-modifier range-vector reuse: fullWindowCount and samplesReadCount are declared inside the per-step loop and only assigned in the `ts == ev.startTimestamp || selVS.Timestamp == nil` block, so a matrix selector with an @ modifier (not wrapped in StepInvariantExpr, e.g. quantile_over_time(scalar(y), x[5m] @ t)) contributes 0 to TotalSamples on steps after the first instead of the full window as before. Measured base vs HEAD: total 39 -> 15. This changes the existing totalQueryableSamples field and prometheus_engine_query_samples_total counter, contradicting the 'unchanged semantics' comment at engine.go:2143 and the new docs; no test covers this shape.
raw: #2 🟠 High: `TotalSamples` silently regresses for `@`-modifier range-vector reuse

claim: The ~900 added TestQueryStatistics table rows are recorded implementation output rather than derived expectations (in-file 'IMPLEMENTATION NOTES ... may need refinement' disclaimer at 1777-1782, 'corrected values'/'Actual behavior' comments at 1539/1544), so the suite pins the 2x subquery overcount as expected (1548 SamplesRead: 2; 1184 SamplesRead: 72 vs TotalSamples: 36) and cannot fail for a wrong implementation. The table also contains exact duplicate cases (sum_over_time(...[30s:30s]) at Unix(90) three times at 1537/1580/1594; sum(max_over_time(...[20s:10s])) at Unix(201) twice at 1553/1586) and a duplicated PHASE 3 banner.
raw: #3 🟡 Medium: the new statistics expectations are recorded output, not derived expectations

claim: countSamplesAfter walks the full floats and histograms slices from the front although it only ever needs the tail (T > maxt-ev.interval); it runs once per step per series in the range-vector hot path (engine.go:2164), so wide windows with small steps (e.g. rate(x[1h]) at 15s over 1s data, ~3600 points) incur a new full-length scan per step. Since both slices are ascending in T, it could iterate backwards or use sort.Search.
raw: #4 🟢 Low: `countSamplesAfter` rescans the whole window on every step of every series

claim: NewChildWithStepTracking calls InitStepTracking, which allocates both TotalSamplesPerStep and SamplesReadPerStep, but no consumer of a subquery child ever reads the child's TotalSamplesPerStep (only SamplesRead/SamplesReadPerStep/TotalSamples are consumed at engine.go:1873-1874 and 2424-2444); it is write-only memory of 8 x numSteps bytes (~700 KB for x[1h:1s] in a 24h range query), where previously NewChild() allocated nothing. Reachable only with promql-per-step-stats and stats=all.
raw: #5 🟢 Low: subquery children now allocate a per-step array that is never read
